comments.body:
Implementation landed in a worktree; change pushed for review (number in a follow-up comment).

## What changed

New `src/rebar/_store/lock_kernel.py` (163 LOC) — THE kernel-mediated exclusive leg, one
selector all three store write-lock probes route through. Contract is total: a real leg is
taken, or `NoExclusiveLegError` is raised and the caller never reaches the mkdir leg.

- POSIX leg: `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`, contention set `{EAGAIN, EACCES}` — the
  same call and the same discrimination as before, verbatim.
- Windows leg: `msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1)` after anchoring the offset, contention set
  `{EACCES, EAGAIN, EDEADLK}`.

Call sites rewired (the ONLY executable changes outside the new module):

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `lock.py:207` `_acquire_fcntl` | `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB)` | `_kernel.take_exclusive(fd)` |
| `lock.py` same | `exc.errno not in (EAGAIN, EACCES)` | `not _kernel.is_contention(exc)` |
| `lock.py:254` `write_lock_is_busy` | `fcntl.flock(...)` | `_kernel.take_exclusive(fd)` + a `NoExclusiveLegError -> return False` branch (it is advisory and documented to fail OPEN) |
| `doctor_locks.py:142/148` `_probe_fcntl` | `fcntl.flock` / `LOCK_UN` | `_kernel.take_exclusive` / `release_exclusive` + `NoExclusiveLegError -> STATE_UNKNOWN` |

Everything else in `lock.py` is docstring.

## AC2 — the `fcntl_held=True` proof, rewritten rather than copied

`fcntl_held=True` stays TRUE under the Windows leg, and the argument is its own. The POSIX
proof rests on `flock` being kernel-mediated on the INODE (hence shared across pid/mount
namespaces on one kernel) and dropped when its holder dies — neither clause transfers to a
platform with no inodes and no pid namespaces. The Windows argument: a byte-range lock lives
on the kernel's file object rather than in the process, so it is enforced against every other
handle machine-wide; and the kernel releases it when the owning handle closes, which it does
for every handle on process termination, abnormal included. Same two properties the
reclamation argument needs, earned differently. Written out in `lock_kernel`'s module
docstring, in `_acquire_mkdir`'s precondition, and in `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`'s parameter doc.

## Adjacent Windows hazard found and fixed in the same path

`lock_owner._pid_alive` probes with `os.kill(pid, 0)`. Python documents that on Windows
`os.kill` understands only `CTRL_C_EVENT`/`CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` and **TerminateProcess**-es the
target for any other value, 0 included. That probe runs on every mkdir-lock contention, so on
Windows reclamation would have KILLED the live writer it was asking about. Narrowed via
`_signal_zero_probes_liveness()`: where signal 0 is not a probe there is no liveness signal,
so the answer is the conservative one and the decision falls through to the branches that need
positive proof (the held leg, or the age ceiling). Strictly narrower — nothing is reclaimed on
less evidence than before.

## Evidence

**RED first, for the right reason.** Before the fix, with `fcntl` hidden, all three use sites
raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'` — the exact sweep symptom.

**POSIX unchanged, measured not asserted.** `test_concurrency_regression.py` +
`test_store_concurrency.py` (storm) + `test_reads_under_sync_contention.py`: **39 passed**
before the change, **39 passed** after. Broader lock/store sweep after: 693 passed, 11 skipped.
`make lint` 0, `make typecheck` 0, complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`, mechanism ratchet
`new=0 increased=0` (no new lock class, no new `.lock` filename).

**Mutation — 7 mutants, 7 killed.**

| # | mutant | killed by |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `take_exclusive` degrades silently instead of raising (THE unsafe two-line fix) | `test_no_leg_acquire_refuses_loudly_and_never_takes_the_mkdir_leg`, `test_no_leg_doctor_probe_reports_unknown` |
| M2 | Windows leg is a no-op (leg "taken", nothing held) | `test_windows_leg_exclusion_survives_the_mkdir_leg_being_removed`, `..._doctor_probe_answers_truthfully` |
| M3 | negated `msvcrt` selection branch | 8 tests |
| M4 | pid-probe narrowing removed | `test_pid_probe_never_signals_where_signal_zero_terminates` |
| M5 | busy probe fails CLOSED | `test_no_leg_busy_probe_fails_open` |
| M6 | doctor probe claims FREE with no leg | `test_no_leg_doctor_probe_reports_unknown` |
| M7 | POSIX contention set narrowed (EACCES dropped) | **survived at first** — see below |

M7 exposed a real pre-existing gap: nothing covered EACCES contention, only EAGAIN, so
dropping it from the set turned a merely-contended lock into a hard write failure unnoticed.
Closed by adding two cases to the EXISTING harness `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`
(`_acquire_fcntl` and the busy probe under EACCES). M7 is killed with them.

Note M2 was NOT caught by the plain two-acquirer test — the mkdir leg alone still excludes.
It is caught by the `dual_window=False` variant, which isolates the kernel leg. That test is
the actual teeth behind the `fcntl_held` proof.

## AC6 in-session check

`grep -nE '(^|[^_[:alnum:]])fcntl\.' src/rebar/_store/lock.py src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py
src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` matches only prose. An AST census of every
`fcntl.<attr>` access across `src/rebar` confirms zero remain in those three files; the only
ones on the write-lock path are `lock_kernel.py:124/146`, both inside `if fcntl is not None:`.

## What is deliberately NOT in this change

- `reducer/marker.py` — same defect, different lock. Existing bug `discrete-unrelative-vervet`
  (`a50a-cac1-af18-42d9`). (I filed a duplicate before finding it; closed as duplicate.)
- `_store/fsutil.sibling_exclusive_lock` — function-local `import fcntl`, so
  `ModuleNotFoundError` at CALL time on the HLC-stamp write path. These are the 4
  `ModuleNotFoundError` lines in the sweep census. It is a BLOCKING acquire and needs a
  blocking take this selector does not expose. Filed as `hyperbolic-humanoid-owl`
  (`658e-a99b-a004-4be3`), a child of the epic, `depends_on` this story.
- `llm/gate_admission.py` — looks unguarded at `:233`/`:259`, but its public entry point
  early-returns at `:319` on `fcntl is None`, so those lines are unreachable. No work.

## Windows-native proof is deferred to CI by design

`test_native_lock_is_visible_across_processes` and `test_native_lock_dies_with_its_holder`
run only where `os.name == 'nt'` and skip on this host. They are the only place the real
`msvcrt.locking`'s two properties are established; the POSIX-host simulation proves rebar's
BRANCH (the stub delegates to the host's `flock`, so exclusivity is real), not Microsoft's
kernel. Those two tests execute in the epic's `sweep (windows)` job.

## `make verify` result and its one wrinkle

`make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=6` reported **9 failed, 19436 passed, 74 skipped in 54m29s**. Eight of
the nine were `GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent gate slots busy`; the
ninth (`test_plan_review_cli_retry::test_cli_retry_is_compatible_with_no_sign`, `assert 11 == 2`)
is the same cause surfacing as a retry count.

**Root-caused, not retried.** `gate_admission._slot_dir()` is the PER-HOST snapshot store's
`locks/` with a cap of 4, and those tests exercise the real admission context manager — so they
compete with LIVE gate runs on the same box. `ps` at the time showed an unrelated session running
`rebar review-plan verminous-zealous-krill` (pids 24863/25001). Two live gates plus `-n 6` workers
exceeded the cap, so the refusals were the cap working correctly and the tests failing to isolate.

A/B on the same host, same selection:

| sources | result |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` (`e510c64dbcb6`), change reverted in place | 20 passed |
| this change | 20 passed |
| remaining 4 previously-failing modules, this change | 51 passed |

All nine pass on this change once slots are free, and the reverted tree fails the same way when
they are not — so the change is not implicated. Filed as `dubious-neutral-duck`
(`bc3e-7f43-2195-4301`), linked `discovered_from` this story: gate-admission tests need their own
slot namespace, because a `make verify` verdict that flips on whether another session is running a
gate is not the local CI contract it is meant to be.

Everything else in `make verify` was green: `make lint` 0, `make typecheck` 0 (763 files),
complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`, mechanism ratchet `new=0 increased=0`.

## Module sizes (cap 800)

`lock.py` 541 (was 522 — docstring only), `lock_kernel.py` 163 (new), `lock_owner.py` 513,
`doctor_locks.py` 466. No split needed.

comments.body:
AC verification pass against the merged tree (worktree detached at 9d5a7278c892, the tip of origin/main; `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` resolves to this ticket).

FIVE of six criteria verified and ticked; AC4 is NOT ticked and the close is NOT run. Detail below.

**AC1 — PASS (ticked).** `pytest tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py -q` -> `10 passed, 2 skipped in 75.73s` (the 2 skips are the `@_needs_windows` native tests, correct on POSIX).

**AC2 — PASS (ticked).** `-k "precondition or pid"` -> `2 passed, 10 deselected`. Substance confirmed by reading the code, not just the test: `_acquire_mkdir`'s docstring (lock.py:334ff) now carries an explicit PER-PLATFORM proof — POSIX `flock` is kernel-mediated on the inode; Windows `msvcrt.locking` byte-range locks live on the kernel file object, enforced machine-wide against every handle and released by the kernel when the owning handle closes, including on abnormal termination. And `lock_owner._signal_zero_probes_liveness()` returns `os.name == "posix"`, so `_pid_alive` returns the conservative `True` on Windows and never calls `os.kill` there — reclamation narrows rather than weakens.

**AC3 — PASS (ticked).** `-k no_leg` -> `3 passed, 9 deselected`.

**AC5 — PASS (ticked).** The three named concurrency suites -> `39 passed in 199.70s`. `make lint` clean (including `scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py`, the repo's own gate for this defect class). `make typecheck` -> `Success: no issues found in 765 source files`.

**AC6 — PASS (ticked), with a recorded caveat about the AC's own literal check.** The in-session grep returns FOUR matches, not zero: lock.py:8, lock.py:201, lock.py:232, lock_owner.py:355. All four were inspected and are RST double-backtick PROSE inside docstrings (the module docstring's dual-window contract, `_acquire_fcntl`'s and `write_lock_is_busy`'s docstrings, and `lock_owner`'s `fcntl_held` note) — the AC's regex matches its own documentation. The substantive condition holds and is stronger than the AC asks: `grep -rnE '(^|[^_[:alnum:]])fcntl\.' src/rebar/ | grep -v '``'` returns ZERO across the WHOLE source tree. Every real call routes through the new `_store/lock_kernel.py` selector.

AC6's post-merge clause was also executed (see AC4 below). It reports 115 real `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'`, not 0 — but every one of them originates in `rebar/reducer/marker.py` lines 33/38/61/67, which this ticket's own Class section declares explicitly OUT of S1's scope (bug `nitro-heavy-bluefish`, the per-ticket archive-marker lock). ZERO come from `lock.py`, `lock_owner.py`, `doctor_locks.py` or `lock_kernel.py`. The store write-lock path — the path AC6 actually names — is clean. Pre-merge baseline for comparison: run 33950878570 (SHA a33333b8, without this fix) had 2593 matching lines, 545 failed / 227 errors.

**AC4 — NOT verified, NOT ticked. This is the blocker.**

At the time of this pass no merged-main CI run had ever executed the native test: the most recent `sweep (windows)` was run 33950878570 at 2026-09-05T06:49:43Z on SHA a33333b8, which does NOT contain 9d5a7278c892 (merged 08:13:39Z). `sweep (windows)` only fires on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`, so the push of the merge did not trigger it.

I therefore dispatched test.yml on main — run **33956014400**, headSha exactly `9d5a7278c892`, job 101279390978, `sweep (windows)` completed `failure` (the job is `continue-on-error: true`; Windows is not yet a declared support target). Full suite: `1518 failed, 16611 passed, 269 skipped, 1375 errors in 5081.80s (1:24:41)`.

The two native tests do NOT appear anywhere in that log — neither in the FAILED/ERROR list nor by name. Under `pytest -q` a passing test prints no line, so their absence is CONSISTENT with passing (the module collected, and `@_needs_windows` is `skipif(os.name != "nt")` so on windows-latest they were not skipped), but it is INFERENCE FROM ABSENCE, not the positive empirical proof AC4 demands. I am not ticking a box on that.

**Discovered work: the story's own test module is 7/12 red on Windows.** Not a production defect — a test-harness portability defect in this story's deliverable:

- 5 ERRORs (`test_windows_leg_write_lock_round_trips`, `..._busy_probe_answers_truthfully`, `..._doctor_probe_answers_truthfully`, `..._excludes_a_second_acquirer`, `..._exclusion_survives_the_mkdir_leg_being_removed`) all fail at test_windows_exclusive_leg.py:169 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'`. `_windows_shaped_msvcrt()` does `import fcntl as host` to delegate its stub to the host's real `flock`. That is the layer-2 POSIX-HOST SIMULATION; on real Windows there is no `fcntl`, so the fixture cannot build. These tests are meaningless on Windows by construction (the real `msvcrt` is present there) and need a `skipif(os.name == "nt")` guard.
- 2 FAILUREs (`test_no_leg_acquire_refuses_loudly_and_never_takes_the_mkdir_leg`, `test_no_leg_doctor_probe_reports_unknown`) fail with the child reporting `AssertionError: acquire succeeded with NO exclusive leg held`. The child hides only `fcntl`; on Windows `msvcrt` is still importable, so the selector legitimately finds a leg and `acquire()` correctly succeeds. The test's premise — "NO exclusive leg available" — is simply false on Windows. This is in fact POSITIVE evidence that the production Windows leg works: the real `acquire()` took the real msvcrt leg on windows-latest.

**Second discovered finding, outside this ticket's file impact:** 1395 of the run's `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` occurrences come from `src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py`, which does a bare unguarded `import fcntl` at :82 and `fcntl.flock` at :92/:98. That is a store module with the same defect class as `marker.py` but I could find no ticket naming it; `lock.py`/`lock_kernel.py`/`lock_owner.py` do not import it, so it is off the write-lock path and does not affect this story's ACs.

No force override was used anywhere in this pass, and no test was weakened or edited.

comments.body:
Correction to one line in the verification comment above, and a note on what happens next.

**The `fsutil.py` finding IS already tracked.** The comment records that `src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py`'s bare `import fcntl` (:82, with `fcntl.flock` at :92 and `fcntl.LOCK_UN` at :98) accounted for ~1,395 `No module named 'fcntl'` hits in the Windows sweep, and says "no ticket I could find". There is one: **`hyperbolic-humanoid-owl`**, open, p2, titled "`_store/fsutil.sibling_exclusive_lock` does a function-local `import fcntl` — ModuleNotFoundError on Windows, on the HLC stamp path". It names those exact lines and adds something the sweep could not show — that this sits on a STORE-WRITE path, since `_store/hlc.py:94` takes that lock around `.rebar/hlc.state`, the hybrid-logical-clock stamp every ticket event needs.

Worth noting WHY the search missed it, since the same miss will recur: the ticket's title leads with the symbol and the import mechanism, not with the error string. A search seeded from the observed failure text (`No module named 'fcntl'`) or from the file path alone does not reach it. That ticket also records that `scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` deliberately ALLOWS a lazy in-function import — correct for collectability, silent about runtime — which is the same shape of gap this story exists to close.

Nothing to do here: it is out of S1's scope and correctly a separate ticket. Recording only so the evidence comment is not left asserting an absence that is not real.

**AC4 remains the only open criterion, and it is now being worked.** The verification correctly declined to tick it: the two `test_native_*` tests appear nowhere in run `33956014400`'s log, and under `pytest -q` a pass prints nothing, so their absence is CONSISTENT WITH passing but is not the positive empirical proof the criterion demands. Inferring a pass from silence is exactly what AC4 was written to forbid.

The blocker is that this story's own test module is 7/12 red on real Windows — a test-harness portability defect in S1's deliverable, not a production defect. Five ERRORs come from `_windows_shaped_msvcrt()` doing `import fcntl as host`, which is the POSIX-host simulation and cannot build where `fcntl` does not exist; two `test_no_leg_*` FAILUREs come from the test hiding only `fcntl` while `msvcrt` stays importable, so the selector correctly finds a leg and the test's premise is false there.

That second one is worth stating plainly because it reads as a failure and is not: **it is positive evidence the production Windows leg works.** The real `acquire()` on `windows-latest` took the real `msvcrt` leg. The test asserts an impossible precondition on that platform, not a broken behaviour.

A fix is in flight — platform-correct skips for the simulation tests and a Windows-aware premise for the `no_leg` pair, changing the tests and not the production lock code, with POSIX behaviour held identical — after which a native result becomes readable by name rather than by absence.

comments.body:
## AC4 follow-up: the test module was not runnable on Windows, so the native proof was unreadable

The production leg merged as `9d5a7278c892` and the sweep shows it WORKING. What was broken was
this story's own test module, `tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py`: 7/12 red on
`windows-latest` in run `33956014400` / job `101279390978`. Both native tests appeared in that log
neither as a pass nor as a failure, so AC4 could only be argued from absence. Verified both defects
against the log before touching anything.

**Defect 1 — five ERRORs, all at `_windows_shaped_msvcrt()` (`:169`), `ModuleNotFoundError: No
module named 'fcntl'`.** That helper is the POSIX-HOST SIMULATION: its stub's `locking` delegates to
the host's real `flock`, which is exactly what makes the layer-2 assertions observations rather than
a mock's say-so — and exactly what Windows does not have. It cannot be built on Windows and must not
be. The `windows_leg` fixture now skips on `os.name == "nt"` with that reason stated. This removes
no Windows coverage: on Windows those same code paths run against the REAL `msvcrt` throughout the
default suite, and the primitive's own guarantees are `test_native_*`'s job.

**Defect 2 — two FAILUREs, `test_no_leg_acquire_refuses_loudly_and_never_takes_the_mkdir_leg`
("acquire succeeded with NO exclusive leg held") and `test_no_leg_doctor_probe_reports_unknown`
(`free` instead of `unknown`).** The premise was false on Windows: the child hid `fcntl` alone, and
`msvcrt` is still importable there, so the selector correctly found a leg. Note this is POSITIVE
evidence for the production leg — the real `acquire()` took the real msvcrt leg on `windows-latest`.
The assertion was NOT weakened. The premise was made true on both platforms: the child now has NO
leg of either kind. `fcntl` is still hidden the module way (`sys.modules[...] = None`, which keeps
proving rebar imports without it); `msvcrt` cannot be hidden that way, because on Windows the
standard library itself imports it at module scope (`subprocess` does) — a `sys.modules` entry would
break the interpreter, not rebar. It is blanked at the ONE handle rebar reads, `lock_kernel`'s
module-level primitive, which is the same seam the layer-2 fixture already patches. On POSIX that
handle is already `None`, so the assignment is a no-op. The premise is now asserted out loud
(`assert _kernel.leg_name() == "none"`), so a future platform with a third leg fails the child
immediately instead of quietly voiding the test — checked by mutation (re-supply a leg ⇒ the child
exits 1 on that assertion).

**Readability — the reason AC4 was unprovable even when green.** The sweep's default suite runs
under `pytest -q`, where a passing test prints nothing. `sweep (windows)` now runs this one module
with `-v` BEFORE the default suite (before, because a failing step stops the ones after it, and this
is the evidence worth keeping), naming each verdict in the log. It gates nothing — the job is
`continue-on-error` — and adds no coverage; it re-runs an already-running module so the proof is
legible. Justified to the mechanism-delta ratchet in place as `mechanism-ok: ci_gate`.

**No production code touched.** POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged: the module is still
10 passed / 2 skipped, the three AC5 concurrency suites are 39/39, `make lint` and `make typecheck`
clean.

Out of scope and NOT duplicated: `_store/fsutil.py:82`'s bare `import fcntl` already has a ticket —
`hyperbolic-humanoid-owl` (`658e-a99b-a004-4be3`), open p2, a child of the epic that `depends_on`
this story.

AC4 stays UNTICKED until the re-dispatched sweep names both `test_native_*` as PASSED.

compiled_state.description:
## Class

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — **384 `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'` plus
4 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'`** in job `100874330553`, roughly 74% of the 510
failures and the single largest class by an order of magnitude.

`lock.py:72-75` guards the **import** (`try: import fcntl / except ImportError: fcntl = None`) but
there is no `is not None` check at either **use** site — `lock.py:207` in `_acquire_fcntl` and
`lock.py:254` in `write_lock_is_busy`. Every store write reaches `_acquire_once` → `_acquire_fcntl`
(`lock.py:491`), so on Windows every ticket write raises.

Two sibling modules DO gate their use sites with `if fcntl is not None:` — `_snapshot/git_fetch.py:79`
and `_snapshot/janitor.py:430` — which makes `lock.py` an **outlier rather than a deliberate choice**.
(`reducer/marker.py` is NOT such a sibling: it guards the import but calls `fcntl.flock` unguarded at
:33/:37, so it shares this defect. That is tracked separately as bug `nitro-heavy-bluefish` and is
explicitly OUT of S1's scope — it is the per-ticket archive-marker lock, not the store write lock in
this story's file impact.)

## THE OBVIOUS TWO-LINE FIX IS UNSAFE. DO NOT TAKE IT.

Skipping the fcntl leg when `fcntl is None` looks like two lines. It silently breaks a documented,
load-bearing invariant.

`_acquire_mkdir` (`lock.py:325-362`) passes `fcntl_held=True` into stale-lock reclamation, and its
own docstring states the precondition verbatim:

> **Precondition (load bearing, hence `fcntl_held=True` below):** this is only ever reached from
> `acquire` AFTER the exclusive `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` leg has been taken … if that owner were
> still alive it would still hold this fcntl lock and we could not be here.

Degrade to mkdir-only and `fcntl_held=True` becomes **a lie**. rebar would reclaim a write lock held
by a **live** process: silent store corruption under concurrency, strictly worse than not supporting
Windows at all, because the failure is invisible instead of loud.

## What a correct fix requires

1. **A real alternative exclusive leg** on Windows — `msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, n)` (or
   `LockFileEx` via `ctypes`) — with the same *kernel-mediated, dies-with-the-process* exclusivity
   `flock` provides. A userspace substitute that does not die with its holder does NOT satisfy the
   precondition.
2. **EVERY store write-lock probe routes through that one selector**, not just `acquire`. There are
   three same-path sites and all three are in scope: `_acquire_fcntl` (`lock.py:207`);
   `write_lock_is_busy` (`lock.py:254`), an advisory zero-deadline probe that fails OPEN and never
   touches `fcntl_held`; and `doctor_locks._probe_fcntl` (`_commands/doctor_locks.py:142,148`),
   the read-only `rebar doctor --locks` probe of the SAME `.ticket-write.lock` — it also calls
   `fcntl.LOCK_UN`, so the selector exposes a release as well as a take. Fixing only `acquire`
   leaves the other two raising `AttributeError` on Windows.
3. **A reworked staleness proof.** The current proof leans on `flock` being kernel-mediated on the
   inode. The Windows leg's proof must be stated explicitly in the docstring and be its own
   argument. If the Windows leg cannot support `fcntl_held=True`, reclamation must be narrowed on
   Windows rather than the flag falsified. Note `lock_owner._pid_alive` uses `os.kill(pid, 0)`,
   which on Windows is documented to **TerminateProcess** the target rather than probe it — so the
   liveness probe must be narrowed on Windows too, or reclamation would kill a live holder.
4. **A test that fails if the invariant is degraded** — the epic's AC5 and `f850`'s AC5, carried
   forward unchanged.
5. **The Windows primitive's capability must be VERIFIED, not asserted.** The whole design rests on
   two properties of `msvcrt.locking`: the lock is visible ACROSS PROCESSES, and the kernel releases
   it when the holding process dies. A POSIX-host simulation exercises rebar's Windows *branch* but
   cannot confirm those properties. They are therefore proved by a `windows-latest`-only test
   (`os.name == "nt"`, skipped elsewhere) that runs in the epic's `sweep (windows)` job: a child
   process takes the leg and the parent must be refused; the child is then killed and the parent
   must succeed. If that test fails, the design is wrong and the story reopens.

## This story GATES the rest of the epic

Until store writes work on Windows the other classes cannot be measured — their tests fail during
store setup before reaching the semantics under test. The bug's ".EXE console-script invocation"
class is downstream of S1: those `CalledProcessError`s carry this `flock` `AttributeError` as
stderr. `S1 blocks` every other child of the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `fcntl` is never dereferenced when it is `None` at any of the three sites in requirement 2;
      a Windows run reaches the same exclusivity guarantee by a different documented mechanism.
